title: The lithium balance: designing a cell forwards
lead: Fit a cell OCV backwards and you get dozens of answers that all sort of work. Build it forwards and you see the design decision behind them.
llms: The lithium balance of a cell in equilibrium: voltage window, N/P ratio, N/Li ratio including formation and prelithiation, aging modes and blended electrodes, each with a small interactive tool.

tabs.name: Voltage window
tabs.teaser: Where the lithium in a cell comes from, and what Vmin and Vmax cut out of the tanks.

tabs.name: N/P ratio
tabs.teaser: Why the anode is built bigger, and the more honest way to measure the margin to plating.

tabs.name: N/Li ratio
tabs.teaser: Why the cathode's first-cycle loss is a bonus in the full cell, and why most cells still end up short of lithium, not of room.

tabs.name: Aging
tabs.teaser: Why aging losses don't add up, and why a cell can lose active material without losing capacity.

tabs.name: Blends
tabs.teaser: Graphite and silicon as two tanks joined by a pipe: who fills first, and how dQ/dV takes the blend apart again.
